# U8 — Complete service operations and integration · Code generation plan

Unit `u8-service-operations-integration` · branch `feature/u8-service-operations-integration` from `origin/develop` (`bf82ed19`, which holds U6's merge, pull request #54) · scope express base · methodology test-after per component · strategy standard · existing suites stay green · an 80% line floor for new code (project.md § Mandated).

## Summary

- Builds: Loop-back 4, beyond the bound (Steps 157–172 on 1–156 as built): work on run 5's 6 Not Met and 4 failing U8 targets. At best 435–438 Met, 0–1 Not Met; no fix makes the stage pass. You chose Retry with fix on 2026-11-22, beyond the bound of three loop-backs. Each target is planned to its own words, not to the clause run 5 named. Every pending digest run counts from the instant U5 recorded, which reverses L3-3's option 1. Every provider's observed state stops every call to it: at sign-in, digests, model jobs and both tools. The PlatformControl store logins demand SCRAM, and every client connection gets a test. The isolation journey asks every list, read, event and asset from one table tied to the host's routes, and the cutover journey shows the abort's order and the rollback's outcomes from Chromium's own reads, wherever a page can show them. The maintenance notice is checked on every address and form of the shell that the tests open, staged and in the realm's own window. Seven choices are yours (L4-2 to L4-8): Q5's storage, where the option the steps follow leaves the approved words unmet and the one that may meet them costs U5's and U6's approvals; an unclear export effect's age; what waiting means for an unclaimed model job; the pinned runtime's libpq, which this stage cannot read; how far the notice's every page reaches; the accessibility phase at 95% of its memory limit; and what is left out. Ten readings are proposed (L4-9 to L4-18). The estimates add up to about 6.25 to 9.75 days of build, about four to five times the Loop-Back Log's figure.
- Touches: U8's own files only: 13 backend and ops files, entry-panel.tsx, U8's scripts, specs and tests. No file U5's or U6's manifest claims changes as written; each option that would is named. Product files: `backend/modules/operations/producers.py`; `backend/modules/summarization/model_runtime.py`, `backend/u8_research_model.py`, `backend/u8_research.py`, `backend/u8_outward.py`, `backend/u8_host.py`, `backend/modules/operations/readiness.py`, `backend/modules/accounts/u8_identity.py`, `ops/src/docsuri_ops/production_wiring.py` and `production_tool.py`; `ops/src/docsuri_ops/u8_platform/platform_profile.py`, `arrangement/installer.py` and `arrangement/verify.py`; `scripts/u8_phases.py`, `scripts/u8_fixtures.py`, `scripts/verify_docsuri_u8.py` and a new `scripts/u8_fixture_assistance.py`; `frontend/src/u8-entry/entry-panel.tsx`. Tests and specs: a new `isolation_routes.json` and a new `operations/test_scram_sites.py`, U8's test files, five files under `frontend/e2e/u8-complete/` (`isolation.spec.ts`, `helpers.ts`, `cutover.spec.ts`, `accessibility-screens.spec.ts`, `migration.spec.ts`) and two jsdom files. Records: the code summary, traceability, the manifest and one step in `u8-cutover-runbook.md`. Not changed: `backend/u8_migrations.py`, `backend/transactions.py`, `frontend/src/App.tsx`, both shared inventories and U7's store. The options that would cost another Unit's approval are Q5's half-precision index (U5 and U6), a new migration for the export age (U5), the notice on the consent step or on signed-in pages (U5 and U6) or on the email cancellation page (U5), and any leak the isolation journey finds in an owner's route file (U6, sometimes U5). `unit-test-instructions.md` gains its own section, written with this plan. No approved design text changes, and the Testing Contract and the boundaries table stay as they are.
- Tests: 45 new backend tests, 5 browser, 1 jsdom, each run once with its behaviour withheld (76 checks); then realms C, D, A, B, U6's two phases and the frontend lanes. Floors and bounds stay. One digest test is replaced, because it asserts the reading this section reverses; the kept-name digest, isolation and cutover tests are rewritten (Steps 159 and 168); and three more existing tests change with their names kept, because they assert the wiring or the list this section changes. The withheld checks are about 83 planted runs, about 20 of them browser runs, on a fail-check realm and four more fresh realms. Step 172 then runs, on the final source: lint, drift and the static checks, the `ops` project's Ruff among them; realm C (operations alone, first); realm D (the plain phases); realm A (`coverage`, `u2-regression`, `frontend`, `build-gate`); U6's `operations` and `coverage` phases on a fresh U6 environment; U2's cumulative Vitest lane, the root suite, the earlier Units' type checks and ESLint that read `src`, and every frontend lane that renders the complete shell; and realm B last (the Construction Verification Command, then `compatibility`, `performance` and `capacity-burst`). The SHA-256 of the 45 paths U8's manifest shares with U5's or U6's is read before the first edit and after the last run. Every count is an expectation until its run is recorded. Runs owed to CI and to later stages stay open.

### What U8 owns

All application code sits at the workspace root. U8 owns no business entity (BR1.6): the records below are U8's own, and every owner change goes through that owner's operation.

- **The complete assembly and its build inputs** (`backend/`):
  - `u8_registry.py`: the registration manifest of BR1.1, with eight contributions, the capability registry of the functional spec, the one navigation set, the lifecycle manifest of BR2.1 and the ModelEvidence pins. Its revision is the digest of all entries.
  - `u8_host.py`: `compose(profile)`, the start checks of Workflow 1, the refused-start state, and the three process roles (`host`, `workers`, `scheduler`).
  - `u8_main.py`: the complete assembly's own entrypoint (`python -m backend.u8_main <role> --profile <manifest>`, BR1.7). `u8_workers.py`: one bounded worker pass over every owner's lanes and the lifecycle control worker.
  - `u8_migrations.py`: the one composed migration chain, used by the realm runner and by the production environment tool alike. `u8_policy.py`: every operating value of U8's requirements, each tied to its source row.
  - `production_boundary.py` (D7: the scheme middleware, host names, headers and caching rules), `log_events.py` (D11: registered JSON log fields and handlers), `request_context.py` (D13 request identifiers, P10 latency summaries) and `maintenance_server.py` (the static maintenance server).
  - By your decisions of 2026-10-24, ResearchWorkspace's production work and the model lane, as `u8_topics.py` does TopicsDigests' live work: `u8_research.py` (the production policy, execution and service), `u8_research_model.py` (the research executor on qwen3:8b) and `u8_model_lane.py` (the shared runtime's lane of one); and PaperAssistance's production source rule for large papers, `modules/summarization/u8_assistance_sources.py`.
  - `modules/summarization/model_runtime.py`, the production model runtime and PaperAssistance's real executor, a new U8 file in PaperAssistance's folder that only U8's lane measures (Step 21).
  - By your decision of 2026-10-24 ("Move, scope tools, test U2"), the complete-realm and production parts of capacity, the production profile, AccountAccess and UsageEntitlements (Step 44): `u8_capacity.py` and `u8_profile.py`; in AccountAccess's folder, `modules/accounts/u8_control_policy.py`, `u8_entry.py`, `u8_mfa.py`, `u8_identity.py`, `u8_lifecycle.py`, `u8_control_http.py` and `u8_local_http.py`; and in UsageEntitlements' folder, `modules/plans/u8_usage.py`. They are U8 files in owner folders, measured only by U8's lane.
- **ServiceOperations** (`backend/modules/operations/`, a new module of the existing `operations` owner):
  - the ledger component: `ledger.py`, `ledger_records.py`, `ledger_cli.py`;
  - `allowance.py`, the email-allowance port's ledger implementation (D12);
  - `observations.py`, `producers.py` and `readiness.py` (BR3.1–BR3.6);
  - `incidents.py` (BR3.7) and `recovery.py` (BR4.1–BR4.10);

  - `dashboard.py` and `http.py`, for C11 with A5;

### What U8 must not change

- Any applied migration file of U1–U7. A correction is a new file. A file the composed chain leaves out stays applied, unchanged, in its own unit's realm (decision "One composed migration chain").
- Any earlier assembly's behaviour: `assemble_journey`, `assemble_u3`–`assemble_u6`, U7's tool, their runners and lanes, apart from one allowlist value per site (BR1.7). The other changes to an earlier unit's code are the ones you decided on 2026-10-22: U2's restore image check and U6's production-only policies. The lifecycle worker's request selection, AccountAccess showing the backups part of an erase as retained by policy, AccountAccess's routers for D1's session lengths and the first sign-in, and U2's key recovery in production (`recover_production`) are, by your decision of 2026-10-24, in U8's own modules. Only what the next paragraph lists stays in U2's files. By your decision of 2026-10-24, U5's live production parts are U8's own (`backend/u8_topics.py`, `backend/modules/accounts/integrations/u8_digest_mail.py`). U5's files hold only seams whose default is U5's built behaviour: the send step's three hooks in `backend/modules/topics/scheduler.py`, `begin_send`'s `admission` in `backend/modules/topics/repository.py`, the shared Resend client in `backend/modules/accounts/integrations/digest_email.py`, and the production profile's mail root in `backend/modules/accounts/services/guarded_entry.py`.

## Decisions carried into code

### Open review points

- **R-08 (NFR design: the request-body limit on the public host).** `read_payload` in `backend/local_browser.py` allows 65,536 bytes only for the fixed loopback test authorities and 8,192 bytes for every other host, so `docsuri.rvnnt.dev` would get 8 KB.
  - The two hosts that browser routes serve join the 64 KB list, one value per site: production's public host `docsuri.rvnnt.dev`, and the composed realm's public stand-in `127.0.0.1:18110` (decision "The composed realm's addresses"). The loopback hosts `127.0.0.1:18200` and `127.0.0.1:18109` reach only the health routes, so their limit never applies to a browser body. Every other host keeps 8 KB.
  - Proved by: an integration test that sends, through the public stand-in, the largest body any mounted route's schema admits and gets it accepted, then sends 65,537 bytes and gets INVALID_ARGUMENT. A unit test checks the production host's entry in the list (Step 40). The complete verification repeats the largest legitimate body through the public stand-in (Step 44).
  - The code summary records the per-host limit as a wording settlement of security-design § 4, for approval at the U8 checkpoint.
- **R-12 (infrastructure: dependency-review).** `dependency-review` in `ci.yml` reports on pull requests only (`if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`). It stays a required check, because required checks gate pull requests. The branch-protection list in the release runbook says "on pull requests", and the code summary records the correction of cicd-pipeline § 3.1's "every push" wording for approval at the U8 checkpoint. No workflow changes for it.
- **R-20 and R-21 (NFR requirements: rotation).** Their fixes are in the approved design (security-design § 7.3, D11). The rotation job's tests prove them: a log folder replaced by a link and a parent replaced by a link are skipped and recorded with nothing in the target touched (R-20); a FIFO under a log's name is skipped at once; a copy-then-truncate run counts the bytes written during the copy; the single call before the truncation is the one accepted, uncounted loss (R-21) (Step 36).
- **The functional design's last review (review-19, R-109–R-115).** The final design text answers each, and code follows that text:
  - R-109, R-110, R-112: Workflow 20 step 5 now clones the pinned models from your home folder, sets the runtime's `HOME` to `models-state/`, and keeps the login account's job definition and home copy until the system job reports every pinned digest at the usual address. The repository's model runner keeps its home copy.
  - R-111: the pin is the SHA-256 of the manifest the runtime stores, checked against the registry's on 2026-10-22, and a changed pin is a new release (BR6.11 (2)).
  - R-113: A7 now says "the digest the release pins for it (ModelEvidence, BR6.11)".
  - R-114: step 4's registered configurations name the tunnel by the name chosen there and the fixed credentials path.
  - R-115: BR6.6 now says the rehearsal size is measured at check time through the operator tool's login.
- **U6's handoffs.**
  - `ApprovedExport` joins `backend/control_worker.py`'s participant table, and its three scope pairs join the lifecycle manifest (Step 17).
  - The hosted key folder is `profile/export-keys/`, as U6 designed and security-design § 6.2 keeps (Step 9).
  - The capacity amendment `ops/src/docsuri_ops/u4_capacity.sql`, whose WAL term reads only `docsuri_u4`, is replaced by A10's one definition (Step 5).
  - `rfc8785`, which `backend/modules/export/rendering.py` imports but which reaches the backend only through `docsuri-ops`, is declared in `backend/pyproject.toml` at the version `backend/uv.lock` already holds, because the complete assembly imports that module directly. This is put to you by this plan's approval (Step 1).

In its place stands a new reconciling file from the same owner, which adds on top of the earlier definition what the later file gave its callers:
    - `accounts/u8_session_authority.sql` replaces `u3_session_authority.sql`. It keeps U2's controls and U3's session authority together, with U3's purposes in one purpose rule and one `guard_session` serving both.

    The chain declares each replacement once (`REPLACED = {left-out file: reconciling file}`), and each reconciling file names the file it replaces in its first line. A left-out file stays applied, unchanged, in its own unit's realm.

It hands each of A6's kinds to a driver and every other kind to U7's `native_adapter`, which refuses A6's kinds as built.

- **The repair exercise** (BR10.3's last item).
  - The tool's `repair-exercise` phase makes a clean checkout of the commit with `git worktree`.
  - There it applies a recorded defect, `tests/u8_service_operations_integration/repair_exercise/defect.patch`: navigation resolution treats a stale capability as available, which breaks BR1.3 and BR3.2.
  - It then runs the affected checks and records which fail. The failing journey's request identifier is followed through the realm's logs to the resolver.
  - Finally it removes the patch, runs the regression test `test_stale_capability_is_never_available` and the affected checks green, and records the exercise in the VerificationRun.
- **Coverage scope.** Every file U8 adds or changes is measured, apart from the runners below, and none is left out to raise a percentage. Each file is in exactly one of two reports, and each report has `fail_under = 80`:
  - `backend/.coveragerc.u8`, in the composed realm's `coverage` phase. It holds every U8 file except the thin macOS adapters, plus the shared and owner files U8 changes.
  - `backend/.coveragerc.u8-macos`, in the `macos-filesystem` job. It holds the macOS adapters.

  As in U6, lines of a changed shared file that only an earlier realm can reach count as missed. U8's own code must carry the total, and Build and Test records each changed file's percentage. By your decision of 2026-10-25, U8's PlatformControl code is in `ops/src/docsuri_ops/u8_platform/`, outside U7's measured package: `.coveragerc.u8`'s ops heading measures it, and its owner heading U7's two seam files, `executor.py` and `native_adapter.py` (Step 44).

  The runners are measurement harnesses, not product code. `.coveragerc.u8` omits U8's runner, `scripts/verify_docsuri_u8.py`, and `.coveragerc.u5` does not list U5's. By your decision of 2026-10-24 ("Move, scope tools, test U2"), `.coveragerc.u2` leaves out U2's runner with its other test tooling (Step 44). The floor checks U8 adds to these runners are pinned by each runner's own tests. U4's runner stays in U4's report, as built.

## Steps

The plan follows the Testing Contract's test-after order: each layer, or each business-logic component, is implemented completely, then its tests are written and run through the layer that holds them. Each test step lists five to eight tests per component, plus the boundary tests the component needs. Every checkbox is ticked as it finishes.

A null would make the discussion read and `resultAvailable` treat the result as gone, and PostgreSQL's `infinity` cannot be loaded into a Python date by psycopg, which U4's reads do (`jobs.py:151-153`, `repository.py:59`). The mark loads in every time zone.
  - This mechanism is put to you with this plan's approval.

### Step 7 — Repository / data access — implement

- [x] **The ledger store** (`backend/modules/operations/ledger.py`, its file layer):
  - `profile/ledger/ledger.jsonl` holds one entry per line: `{seq, prev, kind, at, record}`, chained by the SHA-256 of each entry's RFC 8785 bytes;
  - `head.json` holds the count and the head digest, and `.lock` is the file lock;
  - an append syncs the line to disk, then replaces the head atomically (temporary file, sync, rename, folder sync);
  - on open the chain is verified up to the head. Valid entries beyond the head that chain from it are adopted, with a record. Only a torn last entry is discarded, with a record. Anything else raises `LedgerDamaged`;
  - `copy()` streams the file up to the head, together with its digest;
  - every writer takes the lock.
- [x] **The observation store** (`backend/modules/operations/observation_store.py`): bounded inserts as the operations owner, latest-per-capability reads in one short transaction, and the bounded deletion call.
- [x] **The sign-in limit store** (`backend/modules/accounts/entry_limits.py`): check-and-count of the three limits in the caller's transaction, a failure count in its own short transaction, and expiry of finished rows.
- [x] **Search candidates** (`backend/modules/discovery/u8_search.py`, its query half):
  - by meaning: up to 200 chunks through the HNSW index, with `SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = 200` and pgvector's iterative scan, over eligible chunks of papers that are not withdrawn;
  - by words: up to 200 papers through `lexical_all` with `plainto_tsquery('simple', …)` and `ts_rank_cd`, with their best chunks from the per-chunk `lexical` index;
  - both in the same transaction, and never a read of the whole corpus.
- [x] **The job list** (`backend/modules/research/repository.py`): `list_owner_jobs(owner, kind, cursor, limit)`, newest first on the new index, mapping each job to A2's item.
- [x] **Imports and parity reads.** Each owner's repository gains its A4 writes and an order-independent parity digest over the compared normalized fields: `backend/modules/accounts/repository/` (accounts, identity links), `backend/modules/personalization/` (settings), `backend/modules/corpus/repository.py` (papers, content, embeddings) and `backend/modules/library/` (saved papers).
- [x] **The backup agent's catalogue** (`ops/src/docsuri_ops/backup_agent/catalogue.py`): an append-only, digest-chained file in U8's folder on the volume, holding the fields of the definition in rules.md, with a head, adoption and torn-entry rules the same as the ledger's, and a rebuild from the files present and their ledger records.
- Files: the seven modules above.
- Traces: BR4.3, BR4.6, BR6.10, BR8.2, BR8.3, BR8.10, BR9.17; P1; A2, A4; D2; NFR4.3.

### Step 9 — Business logic: the production profile and the browser boundary — implement

- [x] **The profile (A9).** `backend/u8_profile.py` (new; your decision of 2026-10-24) holds a production loader beside `backend/local_profile.py`'s synthetic `load`, applying the same owner, mode and link rule.
  - **What it reads.** `/Library/DocSuri/profile/environment.json` holds:
    - the mode, the admission, and the current database (the profile's rehearsal database in rehearsal mode, `docsuri_v2` in live mode);
    - the public origin, the listen and maintenance ports, and the backup volume's identity;
    - the maintainer's account reference and the account names;
    - the key folders `export-keys/`, `control-keys/`, `verifier-key/` and `cursor-key/`.
  - **What it refuses (BR6.1).** A root that is relative, under `/tmp`, a link, not owned by the service account or not 0700, and any file in it that is not 0600. It has no expiry.
  - **Who changes it.** Only PlatformControl's profile operation (BR9.15).
- [x] **Owner transactions.**
  - Every connection, synthetic and production, carries `require_auth=scram-sha-256` (D9).
  - The production realm is admitted beside the synthetic ones, with the per-process gates from `u8_policy` (host 12, workers 8, observations 2, maintenance 2).
  - The database-identity check stays as built.
- [x] **Artifact roots.** `backend/artifacts.py` takes production roots under the profile, and the synthetic `/tmp` roots stay.
- [x] **Key folders.** U2's keyring folder, today hard-coded to `/tmp/docsuri-u2-run`, comes from the profile (`control-keys/`), and so does the verifier key (`verifier-key/`). U6 keeps `export-keys/`, and the cursor key keeps `_cursor_key(profile)`.
- [x] **The boundary (D7), `backend/production_boundary.py`.**
  - **The scheme.** The outermost middleware sets the scheme to `https` for a request whose `Host` is exactly the profile's public authority: `docsuri.rvnnt.dev` in production, `127.0.0.1:18110` in the composed realm. Every other request keeps `http`, so it reaches the health routes and no browser route. No `X-Forwarded-*` or `Forwarded` header is ever read.
  - **Host names.** The public authority, `127.0.0.1` and the listen authority; every other host is refused.
  - **Headers.** The built set, plus `form-action 'self' https://accounts.google.com https://orcid.org`, `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` on public-origin answers, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()` and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`.
  - **Caching.** `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` only for files the build manifest lists as content-hashed, and their `.gz` copy for a browser that accepts gzip, with `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. Everything else keeps `no-store`.
  - **Wiring.** `backend/local_host.py`'s `assemble` takes an optional boundary and installs it outermost, leaving the default unchanged for earlier assemblies.
- [x] **The server settings.** Uvicorn runs with `proxy_headers=False`, no `forwarded_allow_ips`, `access_log=False`, `timeout_graceful_shutdown=10`, `workers=1`, `limit_concurrency=32` and `backlog=16`, over plain HTTP on loopback.
- [x] **Request identifiers and latency (D13, P10), `backend/request_context.py`.**
  - Each request gets a fresh UUID in a context variable, never one taken from a header.
  - The identifier goes into the error answer's `requestId`, which replaces the random value at `local_browser.py:51` and the fixed `"boundary"`, `"assembly"` and `"capacity"` values, and into every log line, observation and job accept.
  - A fixed-bucket histogram is kept per route class. A route registered without a class fails the assembly check. Every 5 minutes the host appends one line per class to `evidence/latency/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`: window, class, count, median, 95th percentile, maximum and 5xx count. It writes no identifier or path, and keeps files 14 days.
- [x] **Logs (D11), `backend/log_events.py`.**
  - `log_event(component, event, **fields)` accepts only the registered names with typed values: identifiers, registered keys and numbers. It writes one JSON object with a UTC `ts` in milliseconds.
  - An unregistered field or free text raises `ValueError` in every synthetic profile. In production the line is written without it and a counter records the refusal, so logging never fails a request.
  - Exceptions are logged as type and code location only.
  - Third-party records keep only the logger's name, the level and the template. The root logger stays at WARNING, and `httpx`, `httpcore`, `urllib3` and `psycopg` at WARNING. Uvicorn's access log is off.
  - v2's own processes write `profile/logs/<process>.log` through `WatchedFileHandler`, created 0600.
- Files: `backend/local_profile.py`, `backend/u8_profile.py`, `backend/transactions.py`, `backend/artifacts.py`, `backend/local_browser.py`, `backend/local_host.py`, `backend/production_boundary.py`, `backend/request_context.py`, `backend/log_events.py`; the key-folder sites in `backend/modules/accounts/control_keys.py` and the verifier key's reader.

- [x] **`backend/u8_host.py`.**
  - `compose(profile)`:
    - runs Workflow 1's checks, in order: the root (the loader); an active production restore without `startAuthorizedAt` (read from the ledger); the release running from a root-owned real path under `releases/` reached through `release`; the ledger reaching its head; the key folders, refusing when accounts exist and a folder is missing; the service secrets, refusing and naming the missing one, while a missing provider secret leaves that provider unconfigured; the backup volume as the service account sees it, which only degrades; and the release tag and commit, recorded.

    - registers in dependency order. Each contribution's revision and schema digest are compared with the manifest, and it is activated or marked unavailable with `missing`, `incompatible`, `dependency-unavailable` or `policy-unresolved` (BR1.2). Then every capability is registered and the lifecycle manifest is configured with AccountAccess.
  - **The refused-start state.** A failed check leaves a process that serves only `/health/live` and `/health/ready`, naming the check. It starts no worker or producer and never exits (R2).

### Step 13 — Business logic: the ledger component, the tombstone register and the email allowance — implement

- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/ledger_records.py`.**
  - It holds one typed schema per record kind: ServiceIncident, RecoveryRequest, BackupSet, RestoreVerification, RestoreTombstone, LedgerCopy, RetainedCopy, ProviderActivation, ConsumerInventory, CutoverRecord, MaintainerApproval, MigrationRun, MisfitRecord, MisfitDecision, ParityReport (a reference to the full report file), EmailAllowance (reserve, release, settle), ReleaseRecord (cicd-pipeline § 5.1 step 12) and ReceiptFacts.
  - Each schema holds only registered fields: identifiers, states, times, reason keys, digests, counts and receipt references, never private text (BR3.4, NFR3.9).
  - Entries are events. Each entity's current state is the fold of its events, kept in memory and rebuilt from the chain on open (performance-design § 4).
- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/ledger.py`, the component half.**
  - `append(kind, record, *, expect_revision)` validates and compares the entity's current revision under the lock.
  - Damage makes `operations.ledger` unavailable and refuses dependent writes. The watcher then opens the incident (Step 15).
- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/ledger_cli.py`**, the words of `docsuri-ledger`, run as the service account:
  - `append` takes a record on standard input. A receipt-bearing kind is admitted only with a receipt that PlatformControl's `readReceipt` confirms, and a MaintainerApproval only with a `platform.decision.record` receipt. It works while v2 is stopped (BR6.10).
  - `copy` streams a consistent copy to standard output and prints its digest.
  - `verify` checks the chain.
  - `read` answers a bounded query for the operator tool.
  - `repair`, in person, replaces a damaged ledger from a verified copy streamed in. It keeps the damaged file aside in the evidence folder and records both.
- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/tombstones.py`** (BR4.6).
  - An erase request's tombstone is appended on the first claim of `restore_enforcement`. A retried claim finds it by request and appends nothing.
  - The head (count and digest) is recorded with every evidence that uses it.
  - `newer_than(set)` lists the tombstones a restore replays.
- [x] **The email-allowance port (D12).**
  - The port is `EmailAllowance` in `backend/modules/accounts/integrations/email_allowance.py`, a `Protocol` with `reserve(kind, message_key)`, `release(reservation)` and `settle(reservation)`. The adapters own it.
  - `backend/modules/operations/allowance.py` implements it on the ledger:
    - a digest is reserved only while the UTC day's count of all mail is below 60, and account mail while it is below 90;
    - nothing is reserved once the UTC month's count reaches 2,700;
    - a retry with the same message key returns the same reservation;
    - a definite refusal appends a release, and an unknown outcome keeps the reservation.
  - The composition wires the implementation into the adapters. Neither AccountAccess nor TopicsDigests imports ServiceOperations.
- Files: `backend/modules/operations/ledger_records.py`, `ledger.py`, `ledger_cli.py`, `tombstones.py`, `allowance.py`; `backend/modules/accounts/integrations/email_allowance.py`; `ops/bin/docsuri-ledger`.

### Step 15 — Business logic: observations, readiness and incidents — implement

- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/observations.py`.**
  - An observation is admitted only from the capability's registered producer, with a registered outcome and registered limitation keys, and with no private text, credential, email address, title or content (BR3.4).

- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/readiness.py`.**
  - Each read derives every capability's state from its latest observation and its age, by the table of BR3.2 and the timing of observability-design § 3.2.
  - `/health/live` answers from memory. `/health/ready` reads in one short transaction and never probes during the request.
  - The service is ready only when no required capability is unavailable, unknown or stale, background work runs and storage admission is open. A degraded required capability is named but does not make the service unready (BR3.1).
  - C01 `listCapabilities` returns the public projection for a caller with no session (BR5.9).
- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/producers.py`.** One producer per registry capability, run on timers in the workers' control loop. Each observes once at start, then every renewal interval (BR3.3):
  - **The owners' probes** reuse `backend/local_observation.py`'s `probe_owner` functions.
  - **Export and digests** read U6's `export.status_counts` and U5's delivery counts. Export is degraded once its oldest unknown or accepted effect is older than 24 h, digests once the oldest pending delivery is 2 h late, and each records an error rate over 24 h (BR3.6).
  - **`storage.capacity`** reads:
    - A10's footprint against the budget;
    - the internal disk's `statvfs` against its floors;

  - **`operations.ledger`** is the ledger check, and **`background.work`** finds lanes behind their deadline.
  - **The providers** report reachability, allowance and hold. The model runtime's producer compares each model's digest from `/api/tags` with its pin (`model-evidence-mismatch`), and re-pins the search model with `keep_alive: -1` every 60 seconds.
  - **`platform.status` and `platform.isolation`** use C10 `inspectEvidence`, read-only, and the newest file in the isolation evidence folder (BR3.5).
  - **`operations.cutover`** compares the CutoverRecord with PlatformControl's routing and service evidence.

  - The ServiceIncident machine of the functional spec lives in the ledger, with one open incident per environment and capability. A new signal attaches to the open incident.
  - A tolerance watcher runs every 60 seconds and opens incidents by observability-design § 3.2's rules. It also opens one when job failures correlate with a required capability.
  - An abort or a rollback takes over the live `operations.cutover` incident (BR9.5, BR9.7).
  - An incident resolves only with the evidence of its kind: `capability-available`, `abort-reviewed`, `rollback-copy-settled` or `environment-stopped` (BR3.7).

When the ledger is repaired, the repair records the incident with the time the damage was first found, and the incident then resolves as `capability-available` once the ledger check passes, so the ledger's record of the damage is complete.

So one sender could fill them and block every provider sign-in, or repeat a start and a false answer to send Google or ORCID a token request each time. In the two complete realms, `ArrivalIdentityService` in `backend/modules/accounts/u8_identity.py` counts each start from the stored flows, in the start's own transaction, right after its flow is written:
  - **Who a start counts under.** Every start counts under its client address, read as the sign-in limits read it, but with an IPv6 address counted by its /48. D2's own limits still count IPv6 by its /64. A signed-in start, a link, also counts under its account.
  - **Each address and each account** holds at most 3 open provider sign-ins (unexpired, and pending or exchanging). Within any 5 minutes it makes at most 10 starts that did not complete and 30 starts in all.
  - **The site** holds at most 200 open ones and takes at most 600 starts within any 5 minutes, from guests and signed-in users together. U2's `flow_capacity` is 201 there, so U2's own count only backs U8's up.
  - **A place frees at once** when a sign-in completes, its exchange fails (`unknown`, as built), or it is refused after the provider's answer (`denied`: an identity no link holds, admission, a missing administrator factor, a changed owner, an identity bound elsewhere). A completion refused before its claim leaves the flow as it was.
  - **The same browser** keeps only its two latest pending sign-ins; a third start closes the oldest as `expired`. So a cancel or Back at Google or ORCID followed by another try needs no new place, and two tabs or a double tap still work.
  - **A refusal** is the built busy answer with `Retry-After`: 30 seconds when a place or the site is full; for a count of starts, until the oldest start it counts leaves its 5 minutes; 1 second when simultaneous starts ran out of retries. It writes nothing. No start counts against D2's sign-in budgets.

    - The user message's blocks are `QUESTION`, `PRIOR RESULT` (discussions only) and `SOURCE EXCERPTS`, each a JSON-encoded value, so paper text cannot forge a header.

U1's `generation_options` and `validate_response` there refuse unknown profiles, and extending them would change U1's file, so this duplication is deliberate and no U1 file changes.
    - The answer format allows only the sent locations, and has no limitations field.
    - The answer schema, an Ollama `format`:
      - `summary` of at most 200 characters;
      - `evidence` of at most 4 items, each with a `location` from the sent ones, a `quote` of 8–120 characters, a `claim` of 1–80 characters and a `stance` of the three stances;
      - for novelty analyses only, `assessments` of exactly 3 items `{criterionId, evidence: [index…]}`, each with at most 4 unique indexes.
  - **The answer's checks.**
    - The stop reason and both token bounds, then the field set, the sizes, no control characters, and `validate_output`. A malformed or truncated answer fails with `INVALID_CONTENT` (U4's BR8.1).
    - The token bounds are output tokens at most 1,280 and prompt tokens at most 3,328. The answer must be JSON with exactly the declared fields. Any failure raises `ResearchFailure("INVALID_CONTENT")`.
    - A quote is matched only within its own location's excerpt, after NFKC and whitespace, quote and dash normalisation, and the exact original span is stored.
    - The normalisation also removes soft hyphens.
    - A quote needs at least 20 characters and 3 words, or 8 characters when mostly CJK. It is not only punctuation or digits, and each quote is used once.
    - An item whose quote fails is dropped (U4's BR2.2), and its claim is never shown. With no quote verified, the result abstains with a fixed summary (U4's BR2.4).
    - **Coverage.** `partial` with at least one verified quote. Otherwise `abstained`: the summary is replaced by a fixed sentence, and the excerpts read are kept as quote-less `uncertain` items with a fixed claim. Coverage is never `complete`.
    - The limitations are fixed sentences only. The first always says only excerpts were read; the second says the summary and claims are the model's, with the count of quotes verified (U4's BR8.2). Each is at most 160 characters, in this order:

- [x] **ResearchWorkspace's production execution and service, `backend/u8_research.py` (new; your decision of 2026-10-24).**
  - **The provider interface**, which `LocalResearchModel` implements:
    - `available() -> bool`, cached for 30 s and called only after a cheap check that work is claimable, so the runtime is never polled every second;
    - `run(sources, *, request, deadline) -> dict`, where `request` is `{kind, mode, text, prior}`. It returns output that has already passed `validate_output`, or raises `ResearchFailure(code)`, a terminal failure, or `ProviderWaiting(cause)`.
  - **How each failure ends** (design § 1.4):
    - `RuntimeUnreachable`, `ModelEvidenceMismatch`, a 5xx `RuntimeRefused`, or a `TimeoutError` with no answer (a queue, a reload, v1 ahead, slow generation) raise `ProviderWaiting`, whose `wait_reason` is `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` or `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`; the attempt counts;
    - a 4xx `RuntimeRefused` or `RequestTooLarge`, both our own request, fail with `INTERNAL_ERROR`;
    - a malformed, truncated or out-of-bounds answer, or a failed `validate_output`, fails with `INVALID_CONTENT`;
    - nothing claimable, an unavailable provider or a busy lane makes no claim and spends no attempt.
  - **`ProductionResearchExecution(ResearchExecution)`.**
    - `housekeeping()` runs U4's three recoveries, completes cancellations without the model (U4's BR6.4), and closes refused claims:
      - spent attempts with the recorded `wait_reason`, else `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`;
      - an ended session or context, or refused authority, with `EXPIRED`;
      - an ineligible source with `SOURCE_INELIGIBLE`;
      - while the model is not ready, a job accepted 900 s ago and never claimed with `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, releasing its usage.
    - `execute_next(deadline=…)` claims, runs the provider and completes under one message identifier derived from the lease and fence:
      - a waiting failure cuts the lease to 30 s and records `wait_reason`;
      - a typed failure is completed as `failed` with its code;
      - a moved fence discards the output;
      - another completion refusal is completed as `failed` with that refusal's code;
      - an unknown commit is sent once more and then left to the lease and the outstanding reconcile.
    - The one message identifier is `uuid5(job, f"{leaseId}:{fence}:terminal")`. Exactly one terminal fact can commit per claim, so a failure fact sent after an unknown success commit is refused as an idempotency conflict.
    - A claim refused `CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED` closes the job `failed` with its recorded `wait_reason`, else `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`. A claim refused `NOT_FOUND`, or refused authority (`PermissionError`, `InsufficientPrivilege`), closes it `failed` with `EXPIRED`. A completion refused with any other `ResearchError`, such as `SOURCE_INELIGIBLE` after a withdrawal, is completed `failed` with that code under the same message identifier.
    - `execute_next` returns one of `idle`, `closed`, `cancelled`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `waiting`, `fenced`, `unknown` and `busy`. It catches only the provider's two failure types and the completion outcomes; anything else reaches the lane, which sets it aside as an incident.
    - `step()` runs housekeeping only, so `ResearchWorker.run_once` and any whole-chain run never do model work in production.
    - Completion re-reads exactly the rows the job sent, by version and ordinal, through `research_rows`.
  - **`ProductionResearchService(ResearchService)`.**
    - It takes `PRODUCTION_RESEARCH`, so the server enforces 2,048 bytes and accepts the production policy reference.
    - It refuses a new research, novelty or discussion request with `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` while that capability's latest observation is stale or reads `model-runtime-waiting`. That is one short read and never a runtime call (P7, NFR8.5).
    - A missing observation refuses the same way, because unknown never counts as available (BR3.2).
    - Its scope checks read only each version's identity, through `research_identity`: the paper, its eligibility and its source address.
  - **`PRODUCTION_RESEARCH`.**
    - A `ProductionResearchPolicy`, recognised by its class: `docsuri-production-research` revision 1, production realm only, questions of at most 2,048 bytes, a 150 s lease, 30 s between attempts and a 900 s unclaimed bound.

### Step 25 — Business logic: the backup agent — implement

- [x] **`ops/src/docsuri_ops/backup_agent/cli.py`.** The commands of Workflow 19's table, one command word each, with any further input as bounded JSON on standard input: a catalogue entry for `stream-back`, a decided date with its decision receipt and subject digest for `set-date`, a mount point for `prepare-volume` and `configure`.

  - U8's folder is writable;
  - free space is at or above 64 GiB;
  - the catalogue verifies;
  - `.docsuri-rem1-managed` is absent from U8's folder and from every folder above it up to `/`;
  - the volume is encrypted, asked of its mount point through `adapters/backup.py`'s `available()`.

  It reports the volume's identity.
- [x] **`writing.py`.**
  - It stages, then writes the archive with `adapters/backup.py`'s `write_archive`, which never replaces a file.
  - The written digest must equal the staged one and, for a stream, the sender's.
  - It checks integrity, removes the staging file and completes the catalogue entry with its earliest disposal time: `retainUntil`, a decided date (refused below 14 days, with its receipt recorded), or the backstop.
  - The kind comes only from the command and the source database.
- [x] **`dumps.py`.**
  - `pg_dump -Fc` runs only for the databases its configuration names: production and the rehearsal pattern in v2's instance, and v1's database through its read-only login, for `snapshot` only.
  - The integrity check: the dump's table of contents lists every table seen at dump time.
  - `verify` restores the newest passed live set, or during the soak the newest rehearsal set, into a new scratch database, with `pg_restore --no-comments --no-owner --role <disposable role>`.
  - `rollback-copy` dumps the stopped production database.
- [x] **`reading.py`.** `stream-back` streams one catalogued file with its digest. The caller checks a tar archive's member checksums.
- [x] **`disposal.py`.**
  - `dispose-due` deletes only a regular file inside U8's folder, reached with `openat` and `O_NOFOLLOW`, whose digest still matches, whose disposal time has passed and which the retention floor does not hold. The floor keeps the newest passed set of each incarnation that still exists and the newest verified ledger copy.
  - It sweeps staging files older than one day.
  - A due file the ledger has no record of is deleted and reported for an incident. A ledger claim the catalogue does not show is refused and reported.
  - The in-person commands are `dispose-event`, `set-date` (only to bring a date forward, with its receipt), `dispose-mismatch`, `rebuild-catalogue`, `prepare-volume` and `configure` (BR4.10's order).
  - With low free space as the only failure, deletion still runs.
- [x] **In the realm.** The realm driver runs the same agent against `/tmp/docsuri-u8-run/backup-volume/`. The two volume-level answers it cannot get there (enforced ownership and encryption) come from the realm's adapter, which records that it is a stand-in.

### Step 29 — Business logic: recovery requests and the restore paths — implement

- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/recovery.py`.** The RecoveryRequest machine of the functional spec, in the ledger:
  - only `backup.create`, `restore.verify` and `restore.production` are offered (BR4.1);
  - the schedule may request only the first two (BR4.2);
  - admission takes the ledger's exclusive lock, with BR4.4's conflict kinds, the successor exception, and the rehearsal-database removal's hold;
  - a waiting request holds nothing and expires after 24 hours (the housekeeping lane, Step 35);
  - the idempotency key is the digest of origin, requester, operation, target, expected revision and `submissionId` (BR4.9);
  - an administrator's MFA is checked again at operator start;
  - an unknown outcome is reconciled from PlatformControl's receipt before any other production-affecting operation.
- [x] **Workflow 5, the backup.** `platform.database.backup`, then a ledger copy beside the set. The BackupSet counts only after integrity passes. A failure opens an incident on `storage.capacity`.
- [x] **Workflow 6, the verification.**
  - The disk guard runs: free space, less the source database's size at dump time, must stay above 20 GiB.
  - The register head is recorded, and the agent's `verify` restores into a new scratch database.
  - Through the scheduler's login, the checks run in order: every table present with its rows, the tombstones replayed up to the head with AccountAccess's restore evaluation, and every tombstoned owner absent.
  - The scratch database is dropped and `scratchRemovedAt` recorded. A drop that fails becomes a retained copy with a 1-day backstop, and the verification fails.
- [x] **Workflow 7, the production restore**, the operator in person, through bound steps each shown against its bound:
  1. route to the maintenance server;
  2. stop v2;
  3. take the pre-restore backup (a successor skips this);
  4. recreate, once;
  5. stream the set back into `pg_restore -j 2 --no-comments` as the restore login, with `maintenance_work_mem = 1GB` and two parallel maintenance workers;
  6. replay the newer tombstones through the production environment tool's `restore-evaluate`;
  7. check integrity;
  8. take the post-restore backup;
  9. record `startAuthorizedAt`;
  10. start v2, wait for readiness, and route back.

  The failure paths are Workflow 7's:
  - failed before the recreate: the request ends failed, then v2 restarts on the untouched database;
  - `post-restore-pending`: retried under the same receipt, or on a replacement volume after your retirement decision;
  - `verifying`: the last steps are retried;
  - `held`: a successor on your decision, which takes the exclusion over without a gap only when it starts running; or abandonment on your decision, whose subject lists every remaining passed set, followed by an empty recreate, ending failed only after that receipt, with v2 then started as the decision authorizes.

  The key folders are untouched (BR4.8).
- [x] **Volume retirement (BR4.10).** Your decision; then `prepare-volume`, `configure`, the status check on that volume identity, the profile operation, and ServiceOperations' comparison, in that order. It is refused while a switch or an abort holds the exclusion, and allowed during a rollback's or a restore's wait.
- [x] The operator tool gains `docsuri-ops recovery backup | verify | restore | retire-volume`, each a sequence of bound operations.

### Step 31 — Business logic: the migration tool and the consumer inventory — implement

- [x] **The owners' import operations (A4).** Each owner's import writes through Step 7's repository methods under trusted composition authority, never through a browser route, and validates by the owner's own rules (BR8.2):
  - **AccountAccess.**
    - `importAccount` carries the email, the verified state, the role (`user` → member, `admin` → administrator) and the display name by the decided mapping.
    - It carries a v1 Argon2id hash unchanged when v2's verifier accepts it. A provider-only account gets no password, and anything else is marked reset-required (BR8.5).
    - A deactivated or pending-deletion account is `closed-in-v1`, and a pending or locked one is `unverified-in-v1` or `locked-in-v1` (BR8.13).
    - Emails differing only in case are `email-case-conflict`, and a missing email is `no-email` (BR8.14).
    - `importIdentityLink` refuses `unconfirmed-link` and `duplicate-provider-link`.
  - **Personalization.** `importSettings`.
  - **CorpusContent.**
    - `importPaper` matches the canonical version identity (arXiv identifier without version, DOI, or the canonical key), so an existing paper is linked, not duplicated (BR8.7).
    - It converts the parsed content within the production limits, and refuses with `ineligible-in-v2`, `exceeds-v2-limit` or `content-shape-unconvertible`.
    - Every chunk is embedded again with the pinned model in batches of 16. v1's vectors are never reused (NFR4.4, BR8.8).
  - **Library.** `importSavedPaper`. Version suffixes collapse into one saved paper, reported as `duplicate-by-version`.

  Every operation returns `imported`, `unchanged`, `updated` or `refused` with a reason, plus the digest of the stored normalized fields.
- [x] **The import phases** (`backend/modules/operations/migration/`), run as the service account through `ops/bin/docsuri-migration-import <phase>`, in person:
  - `v1_source.py` reads v1's records from the run's import database;
  - `identities.py` derives each target identity from (v1, kind, source id) as a UUIDv5 (BR8.3);
  - `phases.py` imports in BR8.4's order: accounts, identity links, preferences, papers with content and embeddings, then saved papers. A record whose dependency was not imported is `dependency-not-migrated`;

  - `parity.py` reports per kind the source count, imported, unchanged, updated, skipped by reason and excluded by decision, with order-independent checksums on both sides through each owner's parity read. The report holds no password, hash, token, email or content, and is stored owner-only in the evidence folder (BR8.10);
  - the idempotency pass runs over the same snapshot and must report zero imported and zero updated (BR8.3).

It uses the policy of the realm the run imports into, which in production is `PRODUCTION_POLICY`.

  - **`isolation_gate.py`** reads the isolation evidence folder directly at every phase boundary and at least once per freshness bound during a phase, and interrupts the run on a lapse (BR8.11).
  - **`disk_guard.py`** checks before the import restore and each import phase: free space, less what the run still has to write, must stay above 20 GiB (BR6.6).
  - **`decisions.py`** lists each misfit kind and reason with counts and source identifiers, and records your decision through `platform.decision.record` (Workflow 10). Anything a final run meets for the first time takes archive-only, marked `newInFinal`. A rejected or failed final run, or an abort or rollback after it started, ends the freeze. A decision changed after the latest accepted dry run started invalidates that run for the switch (BR9.2).

### Step 33 — Business logic: the cutover and disposal — implement

- [x] **`backend/modules/operations/cutover.py`.** The CutoverRecord machine of the functional spec in the ledger. Every row's guard and action is the table's, including:
  - the switch's start: your decision, and BR9.2's preconditions, each named when missing (reliability-design § 12);
  - the 4-hour bound from v1's stop, after which only the abort is offered (R8);
  - opening, which needs the approved final report, the first live backup passed, providers verified or accepted unavailable, every required capability available and no open incident (BR9.4);
  - the abort, with v1 serving before anything of v2's is removed (BR9.5);
  - the rollback, with v2's lifecycle outcomes applied to v1 and every v1 session ended before v1 serves, then the database copy, the copy-pending wait with its three exits, and the cancel (BR9.7, BR9.13);
  - settlement, by your decision after the window, under the inventory's dispositions (BR9.8).
- [x] **The soak (BR9.3).** It reads the ledger's evidence over the 7 days: incidents, scheduled backups and a restore verification of the rehearsal database. A new release tag resets its clean period.
- [x] **The restart rehearsal (BR9.16).** It records the receipts of the maintenance route, v1's stop and start from its fixed checkout at its recorded commit, and v1's health and a signed-out page through the public address, together with v1's commit. Any later change to v1's checkout or services voids it.
- [x] **The first sign-in notice (BR9.6).** The profile marks the switch, and the workspace shows MovedNotice (Step 41).
- [x] **The disposal pass (Workflow 14 step 4, BR9.12, BR9.17).** It runs after each scheduled backup and whenever the volume check passes again, never while a switch, an abort, a rollback or a production restore holds the live exclusion.
  - It disposes each place through its one path: the agent's `dispose-due`, PlatformControl's database removal, and your in-person deletion of v1's stores.
  - It records each disposal time from the receipt.
  - A disposal that cannot complete keeps `disposalPendingSince`, is retried, and opens an incident once a backstop has passed.
- [x] **`ops/src/docsuri_ops/cutover/`.**
  - `tool.py` holds the operator commands: `docsuri-ops cutover status | start | open | abort | rollback | cancel-rollback | retry-copy | waive-copy | settle | rehearse-restart`. Each runs its bound operations in order and shows the time left.
  - `preconditions.py` holds BR9.2's evaluation.
  - `disposal.py` holds the pass's orchestration.
- [x] **Cutover decisions (your decision of 2026-10-24, "Add decision commands").** `docsuri-ops cutover decide <kind>` records each approval the cutover commands take (switch, open, rollback, settle and any other `approvalId` they need) in two calls, as the migration decisions do:
  - the first shows the subject and its digest and records nothing;
  - the second carries that digest, renders the subject again, refuses if it changed, and records through `platform.decision.record`.

  The cutover commands then take that approval.
- [x] **Starting the cutover (BR9.1; your decision of 2026-10-24).** `docsuri-ops cutover begin`, in person:
  - creates the CutoverRecord for the installed release's tag;
  - records the profile's named rehearsal database as a retained copy and creates it with `create-disposable`, a template copy with production's CONNECT grants;
  - sets it through `platform.profile.rehearsal-database`, so the ledger knows the database v2 runs on;
  - restarts v2's three roles, and reports readiness after waiting up to 10 minutes.

  `docsuri-ops cutover check` runs the soak's evaluation and moves the record between rehearsing and ready-to-switch, naming what is missing. `status` answers `none` when no record exists.
- [x] **Readiness waits (your decision of 2026-10-24).** After `start-v2` at the switch, after opening's restart, after `cutover begin` and after `migration accept`, readiness is polled every 5 s for up to 10 minutes, as the release command's own wait does.
- [x] **Opening applies admission (BR9.4; your decision of 2026-10-24).** `cutover open` restarts v2's three roles through `platform.service.control` after the admission change, and requires readiness before the record moves to switched. Otherwise the switch aborts, and admission returns to maintainer-only.
- [x] **The rollback's return to rehearsal (BR9.7, BR9.15; your decision of 2026-10-24, "Create a fresh rehearsal database").** Opening removed every rehearsal database. So at v1's serving, the rollback (`ops/src/docsuri_ops/cutover/tool.py`):
  1. names a new rehearsal database with the instance's naming, and records it as a retained `rehearsal-database` copy of the cutover before anything is written, so a retry uses the same name;
  2. creates it empty with `create-disposable`;
  3. sets it through `platform.profile.rehearsal-database`;
  4. only then sets admission maintainer-only and mode rehearsal, clears the provider approvals and ends the freeze.

  The record's accepted dry run is cleared at that step, because its database is gone. So the soak starts again only after a dry run accepted after the rollback (functional spec, the CutoverRecord rows for `rolled-back`). Until then v2 stays stopped, on a profile that loads.

  If any of these steps fails, v1 keeps serving, the cutover stays rolling-back, and the copy does not start. The rollback's retry runs the serving step's missing steps first, each replaying its receipt by its key, and only then the copy.

  **A rollback is never blocked by the database count** (your decision of 2026-10-25, "Never block a rollback"). Its start is never refused for NFR8.15's count. At its serving step, before naming its new database, it removes the rehearsal databases this cutover's opening left pending, each through PlatformControl's database removal, with their sets disposed after them. A removal that fails leaves v1 serving and the step retryable by running `rollback` again. Only the new database's creation is then counted, and it always fits.

  **The soak waits for v2's readiness** (the fix pass of 2026-10-25, confirmed by your decision of 2026-10-25, "Confirm: no soak until ready"). When the soak would start from `rolled-back`, v2's roles start and readiness is waited for. A v2 that never becomes ready starts no soak: the record stays `rolled-back`, the answer is `v2-not-ready`, and `cutover check` or `docsuri-release verify` tries again.
- [x] **An accepted dry run disposes the database it replaces (functional spec, the CutoverRecord row "a dry run is accepted"; BR9.17).** Once the profile names the accepted run's database and v2's roles have restarted on it, the rehearsal database the profile named before is removed and its rehearsal sets disposed, in the order profile, database, sets. That database may be an earlier accepted run's, `cutover begin`'s or a rollback's. A removal that cannot complete stays pending for the disposal pass. So repeated dry runs stay within NFR8.15's two rehearsal databases. Each creation (a dry run's start, `cutover begin` and the rollback's) is admitted only while fewer than two rehearsal databases are open, counted from the ledger's open retained copies, and refused with `rehearsal-database-limit` before anything is written.
- [x] **The production cutover's wiring** (`ops/src/docsuri_ops/production_wiring.py`; your decision of 2026-10-24):
  - `verification` reads `control/releases/verification-run-<id>.json` (`verificationRunId`, `releaseTag`, `commit`, `passed`), as the release command records it;
  - `lifecycle_outcomes` and `v2_writes` come from `RollbackOutcomes` over production's owner transactions;
  - `v1_accounts` and `v1_states` read v1's accounts read-only at the `v1Sources` address;
  - `activation` is ProviderActivation over the ledger;
  - `fail_final` is the migration tool's `fail`.
- Files: `backend/modules/operations/cutover.py`, `retained_copies.py`; `ops/src/docsuri_ops/cutover/` (four modules, plus the decision command, and by your decision of 2026-10-24 `begin`, `check`, `status`'s `none`, `open`'s restart, the readiness waits, the rollback's return to rehearsal and the accepted dry run's disposal); by your decision of 2026-10-24, `ops/src/docsuri_ops/production_wiring.py` (the production cutover's wiring) and `ops/src/docsuri_ops/u8_platform/u8_protocols.py` (the rehearsal database's change while a rollback runs; its package by your decision of 2026-10-25).

### Step 35 — Business logic: the standing job, the isolation check, log rotation, the maintenance server and the root jobs — implement

- [x] **The standing job** (`ops/src/docsuri_ops/standing/`), run as the scheduler account by `ops/bin/docsuri-standing`. It runs one lane per task (reliability-design § 11), never overlapping a task with itself. A turn that comes while its lane still runs is skipped with `skipped-overlap`, and a skipped backup or verification pings `/fail`.
  - **`heartbeat.py`** probes every 5-minute slot: the public `/health/ready` and the local one, each within 10 s. **`availability.py`** appends the slot's line (`slot`, `up`, `reason`) to `availability/YYYY-MM.jsonl` (Seoul month), syncs it, and computes the month's figure over every scheduled slot, a missing slot counting as down.
  - **`healthchecks.py`** sends a ping with no body to each check's address, with a 10 s limit, and `/fail` on a down slot. The addresses are read from `scheduler/`. In the realm the pings go to a local stand-in.
  - **The lanes:**
    - the agent's status check and the isolation check every 5 minutes;
    - the 04:00 backup with its ledger copy, then the disposal pass;
    - the 05:00 verification on Sundays and on any day an erasure waits;
    - hourly housekeeping (`housekeeping.py`): request expiry, pruning observations older than 14 days, and pruning the availability record past 13 months.

    Each of the backup and verification lanes catches up at start when its run is overdue (R4).
  - **The ledger copy** pipes `sudo -n -u _docsuri_v2 docsuri-ledger copy` into `sudo -n -u _docsuri_r1t_backup docsuri-backup-agent ledger-copy`, so the copy reaches the agent only as a stream.
- [x] **The runtime isolation check** (`ops/src/docsuri_ops/isolation_check.py`, with `isolation_macos.py` as its tool adapter), run as root with no argument. It checks the items of security-design § 6.8:
  - programs;
  - rule and configuration files against `control/arrangement-manifest.json`, honouring a valid in-progress marker;
  - accounts;
  - the database;
  - the filter;
  - the backup volume;
  - `isolation-backups`;
  - boot items, with stop records.

  Each item has its own time limit, and an item that hangs is unknown, so the whole check ends within 60 s. The `otool -L` result is kept per program digest. Each run writes one JSON file in `evidence/isolation/` and deletes its own files older than 14 days.
- [x] **Log rotation** (`ops/src/docsuri_ops/logrotate.py`), the root job at 03:00, over the fixed, root-owned folder list of observability-design § 7:
  - every folder is opened one component at a time from `/Library/DocSuri/` with `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`, checking the owner at each step;
  - files are opened with `openat` and `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, then checked through `fstat`: a regular file, one link, owned by the folder's account;
  - v2's own logs are moved aside with `renameat`;
  - files launchd holds open are copied to the end, written with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` (owner and mode 0600 set on the descriptor), checked once more counting the bytes written during the copy, and truncated through the same descriptor after confirming device and inode;
  - PostgreSQL's dated files are only deleted after 14 days;
  - each run writes one summary line to `control/logs/`.
- [x] **The maintenance server** (`backend/maintenance_server.py`) answers `GET` and `HEAD` only. It serves the notice at every address except `/privacy` and `/terms`, where it serves the legal pages' static copies, all from the release's build. It sets no cookie, sends security-design § 4's headers with `no-store`, and has no application or database dependency.
- [x] **The root jobs.**
  - `ops/src/docsuri_ops/pf_loader.py` (`docsuri-pf-load`) loads `/etc/pf.anchors/org.docsuri.v2` under `com.apple/*` and enables the filter.
  - `ops/src/docsuri_ops/backup_unlock.py` (`docsuri-backup-unlock`) unlocks `DocSuri_Backup` with the System keychain's passphrase at boot and every 60 seconds while the volume is present and locked.
- Files: `ops/src/docsuri_ops/standing/` (six modules plus `macos.py`), `isolation_check.py`, `isolation_macos.py`, `logrotate.py`, `pf_loader.py`, `backup_unlock.py`; `backend/maintenance_server.py`; `ops/bin/docsuri-standing`, `docsuri-isolation-check`, `docsuri-logrotate`, `docsuri-pf-load`, `docsuri-backup-unlock`.

  How it runs:
  - **Plan mode** lists every change, with its difference, and changes nothing. A second run changes nothing.
  - **Order.** Each phase checks its own result before the next starts.
  - **By hand.** Every step that needs your eyes or a login (Cloudflare's dashboard, healthchecks.io) is a `checklist.py` item the installer waits on and records without its secret.
  - **Secrets.** Every password is generated from 32 random bytes by root, straight into its holder's file or the System keychain (`keychain.py`).
  - **The keyring start and its snapshot (your decisions of 2026-10-24, "Add a key snapshot step", and of 2026-10-25, "Start it at install, U8 snapshot").** The installer creates no key: its phases only make the key folders. v2's first start creates the verifier key once its database answers (Step 11), and the database first answers when phase 7's `first-rehearsal-database` item (the operator tool's `cutover begin`) creates it and restarts v2 on it. Once that start has created the key, and before any account exists, phase 7 stops v2's three roles, runs the production tool's `control-key-start`, and starts them again. So every sign-in secret production holds uses the started key, and production key recovery has a snapshot to recover from. A second installer run finds both in place and changes nothing.
  - **The installation log** records each step's name and outcome, never a secret.
- [ ] **`verify.py`, the installation's verification.** When the installer runs in person as root, it executes the checks that need the real arrangement, records each result in the installation log, and ends with the isolation check (Workflow 20 step 11). The logic is tested here with fakes, and it runs for real at the installation, as the section "Completion and evidence boundaries" lists.

Preflight reads GitHub's public check runs and records the VerificationRun; it checks the annotated tag on `main`, no active restore, switch, abort or rollback, isolation passed within 15 minutes, disk room, and the performance phase's thresholds (6 GiB of memory available from `vm_stat`, and fewer than 60 requests a minute over 15 minutes).
  - **Step 2.** It stages `releases/<tag>/` with decision "The release environment", downloads the workspace build and checks its SHA-256, runs `otool -L`, and reads the arrangement version, refusing a lower or unknown one.
  - **Step 3.** The performance phase runs from `releases/<tag>/`.
  - **Steps 4–6.** Maintenance (live mode only), stop, and the backup after writes stop.
  - **Step 7.** The release's own installer runs only for a higher arrangement version, under the marker.
  - **Step 8.** Each owner's new migrations run through the production environment tool.
  - **Step 9.** The links are swapped atomically: a new link is renamed over the old one.
  - **Steps 10–12.** Start and the probe journey, routing back, then the record. The marker is removed, and every folder neither link points to is deleted.

  Every way out clears the marker and records the arrangement's state (§ 5.4). `docsuri-release rollback` switches the links back behind the maintenance notice while `release-previous` points to a kept release. An install holds the live exclusion in the ledger (BR4.4).

It restores only the keyring's missing files, its record and its start marker, from U8's keyring snapshot, by the snapshot's exact digest and generation. It refuses another folder, a missing snapshot or a divergent current file before it writes anything, and never writes the verifier. U2's `control_key_recovery.py` is as built, with U2's test folder and snapshot format;
  - `control-key-start` (your decisions of 2026-10-24, "Add a key snapshot step", and of 2026-10-25, "Start it at install, U8 snapshot"), in `u8_verifier_key.py`, run in person while v2 is stopped and refused while it runs:
    - It starts the control keyring once, with U2's own `ControlKeyring.rotate` on the profile's `control-keys/`. That writes a new active key and the start marker, and keeps the key derived from the verifier key for reading only.
    - It then writes U8's keyring snapshot under `control-keys/`: the keyring's record and its marker's run, with no verifier. The snapshot is written once and never replaced.
    - Run again, it takes only a snapshot that is missing; with the keyring started and the snapshot present it changes nothing. So a start cut short between the rotation and the snapshot is completed by running the word again.
    - It answers `control-key-start-refused`, writing nothing, while v2 runs or when the profile's folders fail their owner and mode checks.
    - Phase 7 of the installer runs it once v2's first start has created the verifier key (above). A verifier replacement needs no new snapshot, because the snapshot holds no verifier.
    - The sudo rules list it as an in-person invocation (`arrangement/render.py`'s `PRODUCTION_TOOL_WORDS`), and the tool's own list (`CONSEQUENCES`) states its consequence;
  - AccountAccess's `replace-verifier-key`;
  - `readiness-evidence`, which records PaperAssistance's reviewed real-model evidence marker.

  Each runs against the production profile with that owner's stated consequence.

  - Builds: the agent's status lists each catalogued file that is not yet disposed of, by record id, kind and disposal point. The backups evidence names each of them, so a total above the 32 listed holds an erasure's backups scope (`volume-files-over-bound`) instead of leaving a file unnamed (NFR3.14, BR2.5), until disposal or recording brings the total back within the list. In production, an erasure's backups scope also holds while the latest status is missing, stale or unusable (`agent-status-unrecorded`, or `agent-status-stale` for an old one). A status is usable only when its catalogue verifies, its volume check has no finding but low free space (`deletionAllowed`) and it carries the standing job's ledger comparison. So a backup volume that is unmounted, unreadable or of another identity, a damaged catalogue, an agent that does not answer, or a status recorded while the ledger could not be read holds every production erasure until the next usable status. A realm without a usable status records `agentStatusRecorded: false` and names no volume file (Steps 62(e), 64(f), 66(f)).

- **L1-53, held mail.** You chose "Refuse up front when held".
  - Built:
    - **What is refused.** While no account mail can be sent, registration and the reset, verification, reactivation and email-change requests answer 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with message key `account-mail.unavailable` and no wait. The screen shows '지금은 이메일을 보낼 수 없습니다. 나중에 다시 시도해 주세요.', which names no time, because neither a hold nor an outage has a known end.
    - **When it is refused.** The option you chose names a Resend that is held, down or unconfigured: the gate's `resend` state is `held` (a first effect waiting, or declined) or `unavailable` (Resend unconfigured), production's account mail is `HeldAccountMail` (Resend unconfigured, or ServiceOperations unavailable), or Resend is down, with `provider.resend` reading unavailable as 운영 shows it, from the newest observation of L1-11's probe or the passive check (Step 53(g)). The refusal comes after the replay check, so a replayed operation keeps its first answer, and where L1-10 checks the limit, before any account read (on the email change, before anything is read by the new address); it is alike for every address and records nothing but D2's attempt count.
    - **What keeps its acknowledgement.** The signed-in email change also refuses a message held at delivery. A signed-out request has already answered when its message is held at the sender, for its one recipient (a rehearsal recipient other than you) or after Resend's tries (L1-69), so it keeps its acknowledgement: refusing it would tell a mailed address from an unknown one (U2's NFR4.8). A message whose tries ended unknown may still arrive, and its link still works.
    - **How an outage is timed.** One failed probe is enough: no answer within 5 s, or a 5xx, marks Resend unavailable (L1-11). From then on every registration, reset, verification, reactivation and email-change request is refused until a later probe finds Resend serving, so even a moment's outage stops all account mail for up to 300 s, the next renewal. An outage meets Resend's tries only while no observation shows it: before a probe records it, at most one renewal (300 s in production), and once its newest observation is older than 900 s and reads stale. The four signed-out requests' messages then meet Resend's tries at the sender, after their answer, and only the email change refuses.
  - Amends: reliability-design § 10's Resend row ("the message fails plainly"), with BR7.2 and NFR7.12, which Step 104(b) reads as: account mail fails plainly at the limit, while none of it can be sent (held, Resend unconfigured or Resend observed down), at the first sign-in's forced reset, and for the email change at delivery; a signed-out request answers before its message is sent (L1-69), so its acknowledgement stands whatever becomes of the message at the sender: held for its one recipient, after Resend's tries, or over the allowance. As at L1-10's limit, the built acknowledgements of the four signed-out requests give way while no mail can be sent; BR2.1 already asks for a truthful service-wide delivery failure and is not amended.
